metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — Kaspa RPC data boundaries
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Internal review of the pinned Rusty Kaspa implementation. No current-network or universal API capability claim. Advanced RPC concepts remain outside introductory Study; independent editorial review is unassigned and difficulty is provisional.
metadata.attribution: Original Geek Protocol questions referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa sources; no source prose or code imported.

questions.prompt: In the cited Kaspa GetBlocks handler, which flag combination returns InvalidGetBlocksRequest?
options: include_transactions true with include_blocks false
include_transactions false with include_blocks true
Both flags false
Both flags true
questions.funFact: Transactions cannot be requested without their containing blocks in this handler. The rejected flag combination is a request-validation error, not an empty successful result.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: A client pages from an existing low_hash with the cited Kaspa GetBlocks handler. How is that starting hash treated?
options: It is always excluded from the response
It is included at the beginning of block_hashes
It is replaced by an unrelated random hash
It is returned only if it is a transaction ID
questions.funFact: The handler prepends low_hash to the returned hash sequence. A paging client must account for this inclusive cursor rather than assume every returned hash is new.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: What does the cited Kaspa GetBalanceByAddress handler return when the node has no UTXO index enabled?
options: A successful zero balance for every address
The total supply as the address balance
A NoUtxoIndex error
An instruction to reveal the wallet seed
questions.funFact: The handler checks the node capability before reading balances and returns NoUtxoIndex when it is absent. An unavailable balance query must not be displayed as a successful zero balance.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: With its UTXO index enabled, how does the cited Kaspa GetUtxosByAddresses handler respond during a transitional IBD state?
options: It silently reports an empty UTXO set
It returns a wallet private key
It disables consensus validation for the query
It returns ConsensusInTransitionalIbdState
questions.funFact: The handler explicitly refuses this read during the unstable initial-block-download transition. Having an index enabled does not remove the separate consistency guard.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: Which assumption does the cited Kaspa GetUtxosByAddresses implementation explicitly warn clients against?
options: Assuming returned entries follow the requested address order
Reading the address attached to each returned entry
Allowing an address to have multiple unspent outputs
Recognizing an outpoint by transaction ID and output index
questions.funFact: The source notes that its entry order does not match the request-address order. Clients should associate results using their identifying fields instead of positional pairing.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: In the cited Kaspa GetBalancesByAddresses handler, what balance value is built when an address has no entry in the returned balance map?
options: An automatic numeric zero
None, preserving an absent optional value
The maximum native coin supply
The balance of the preceding address
questions.funFact: The lookup uses get followed by copied, so a missing map key produces None. This handler does not replace that absence with zero or prove a particular reason for the missing entry.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: When does the cited Kaspa SubmitTransaction handler pass Orphan::Allowed to transaction submission?
options: Whenever any RPC client is connected
Whenever the transaction pays a fee
Only when unsafe RPC and the request allow_orphan flag are both enabled
Only when both of those settings are disabled
questions.funFact: The effective permission is the logical AND of the node setting and request flag. In safe RPC mode a requested allowance becomes Orphan::Forbidden; the permission alone does not guarantee acceptance.
questions.attribution: Geek Protocol original question referencing ISC-licensed Rusty Kaspa code; source prose and code are not imported.

questions.prompt: With unsafe RPC enabled, what happens if the cited EstimateNetworkHashesPerSecond request exceeds the configured pruning depth?
options: The handler reconstructs all pruned history
The window is silently reduced to one block
The safe-mode maximum is the only remaining restriction
The handler still returns WindowSizeExceedingPruningDepth
questions.funFact: Unsafe RPC removes the separate safe-window restriction, but the next pruning-depth check is unconditional. It does not grant an estimate over a window beyond that configured boundary.
